source.title: Fear, defense, and emotion: A neuroethological understanding of the negative valence research domain criteria.

confidence_rationale: Current (2024), authoritative statement of the Predatory Imminence Continuum (PIC) by its originating lab, explicitly mapped onto NIMH RDoC negative valence constructs. High source quality (senior-author synthesis of a 40-year research program) and high mapping fidelity to the design question (the PIC's mode structure is exactly the kind of threat-graded behavioral-category framework SD-hazard-aware-policy-decomposition needs to ground its selection rule). Not the top confidence score because it is a review/synthesis rather than new primary data.
failure_signatures: If REE's redecomposition selection step, once built, produces a single continuously-varying blend across all harm magnitudes with no qualitative change in candidate-preference pattern near high imminence, that would be inconsistent with PIC's core claim that defense is organized into qualitatively distinct MODES (not a single continuous response curve) -- the functional form should reproduce at least a coarse mode-like structure, not pure linear blending.

If defensive-mode-like behavior in REE never changes as a function of anything resembling proximity/imminence (i.e. the same tile-selection pattern regardless of z_harm_a magnitude), that would indicate the harm-valence signal is not functionally connected to selection at all -- the specific gap this lit-pull was commissioned to help close.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The Predatory Imminence Continuum (PIC) organizes antipredator defensive behavior into distinct MODES that vary along the psychological/spatiotemporal closeness of a predatory threat (pre-encounter, post-encounter, circa-strike), corresponding to increasing negative-valence intensity (roughly: anxiety, fear, panic). PIC modes correspond closely to RDoC's Potential Threat and Acute Threat negative-valence constructs. Amygdala activity is causally implicated in both the subjective emotional state and the defensive behavior across this continuum.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the primary theoretical scaffold for SD-hazard-aware-policy-decomposition's design question: real defensive systems do not pick a response as a pure linear function of threat magnitude, they organize responses into a small number of qualitatively distinct MODES keyed to imminence, with mode identity itself doing much of the selection work. For REE's `_apply_policy_decomposition`, this argues against a purely continuous, single-scalar harm-weighting of candidate re-tilings and toward a selection rule that is sensitive to which REGIME (something like distal/pre-encounter vs proximal/circa-strike) the current `z_harm_a`/`threat_scale` reading falls into, in addition to any graded weighting within a regime.
mapping.mapping_caveat: PIC is a description of WHOLE-ORGANISM response-mode selection (freeze/flee/fight/vigilance), not a description of how a re-planning/redecomposition subsystem selects among candidate sub-plans. The mapping to REE's specific junction (choosing among surviving policy tiles after a mid-execution abort) is by analogy -- REE has no direct architectural equivalent of 'defensive mode' yet, and building one is exactly the substrate work this lit-pull is meant to inform, not something already validated in REE.
mapping.source_context: Theoretical/synthesis review spanning rodent defensive-behavior neuroscience and human RDoC negative-valence research; senior-author (Fanselow) statement of PIC as of 2024.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality, current, authoritative theoretical synthesis. Mapping fidelity moderate-high: the PIC's core claim (mode-organized, imminence-graded defense) is directly what the design question needs, but transfer risk is non-trivial because REE has no existing 'defensive mode' construct to map onto -- this paper grounds the CONCEPT, not a REE-specific implementation detail.
